title: Make single activity delivery reuse the batch policy check
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

The activity authorization checks exist twice: `record_activity` (host/src/native.rs ~640–717) and `check_activity_policy` (host/src/native.rs ~977–1020). They agree today, but a future fix to one (for example the trail-transition and format-character fixes) can silently miss the other and re-open a worker-trust gap on one delivery path. Make `record_activity` call `check_activity_policy`, and add a test that feeds the same hostile event through both paths and expects identical outcomes. Take this after the other two 2026-10-16 security-review items (ordering, not a block). The wider delivery-path dedupe stays in P3 brwr-o1l.

From the 2026-10-16 security review (read-only, host code at main c908fc5; nothing serious, these are hardening items), not separately verified: confirm with a failing test before fixing. Line numbers are from c908fc5; re-check after step 6.6.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test reproducing the reported gap fails before the fix and passes after; the full Rust and extension suites are green. If the test shows the finding is wrong, close as not reproduced with the reason.

title: Strip Unicode format characters from logged page text
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`safe_markdown_line` replaces control characters but lets Unicode format characters through. A page title containing U+202E (RTL override), U+200B–U+200F, U+2066–U+2069, or U+FEFF reaches the daily log and can make one entry look like another (for example, a reversed URL-like title). Obsidian syntax such as `%%`, `==`, and `#tag` also passes. This pre-dates the overnight work (M1). Strip or replace Unicode category Cf in row text (titles and any presentation text), keeping the hex marker payload byte-exact. Also decide whether to neutralize `%%` comments and `#` tags in titles.

From the 2026-10-16 security review (read-only, host code at main c908fc5; nothing serious, these are hardening items), not separately verified: confirm with a failing test before fixing. Line numbers are from c908fc5; re-check after step 6.6.

title: Restrict trail transitions to Chrome's known values
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`trail.transition` in delivered activity events is accepted as free text up to 64 characters (host/src/capture.rs ~136, activity shape check). Today it is stored only inside the hex marker payload, but the step 6.6 index reader will read it, so an unvalidated worker-supplied string becomes index input. Reject (terminal `rejected`, not retryable) any transition outside Chrome's webNavigation TransitionType set: link, typed, auto_bookmark, auto_subframe, manual_subframe, generated, start_page, form_submit, reload, keyword, keyword_generated. Also allow whatever qualifier encoding the worker already uses, and make the 6.6 reader tolerate older entries.

title: Replace the hand-written SQLite snapshot with an incremental real-SQLite index
description: Step 6.6 (host/src/index.rs) emits index.db with a custom SQLite file-format writer (build_sqlite) and keeps the real cache in index-state.json. Every publish re-derives all artifacts from the full event history, serializes the whole-history JSON state (64 MiB cap, after which index updates fail), and rewrites the entire index.db. Both are whole-file atomic replacements, so concurrent host processes are last-writer-wins. The writer supports no secondary indexes or overflow records, so M3 FTS5 cannot be built on it. Move to rusqlite with incremental upserts inside transactions (WAL, busy timeout), keep the daily log authoritative and brauser reindex as the full rebuild, and drop the hand-written writer and the whole-history JSON cache. Keep the existing 6.6 tests (hostile title, case-colliding ID, external edit replaced, heavy-use day with no file write, rollup bounds) passing.
acceptance_criteria: index.db is written through rusqlite with per-delivery incremental updates (no full re-derive or full-file rewrite on a normal delivery); a year-scale fixture stays within bounded per-delivery time and has no 64 MiB ceiling; build_sqlite and the whole-history JSON state are removed or reduced to a bounded watermark; brauser reindex reproduces the same tables; all step 6.6 tests and full suites green.

Stdin EOF must still end the process and kill any child.

title: Make first-tool setup one coherent transaction
description: Cookie's own proposal, only after the plan work. Let a new user choose Jira, SharePoint/OneDrive or GitHub first, enter the exact tenant and any required scope, then request Chrome access and native-confirm the site plus starter together. Roll back a newly acquired grant on cancel; retain it when notes or another site purpose already needs it.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can pick a tool, scope it, and confirm site plus starter in one native confirmation; cancel rolls back a newly acquired Chrome grant; tests cover rollback and retained-grant cases.
notes: When composing first-tool setup, show installed GitHub PR and issue owner scopes separately; do not infer one shared editable scope when their policies differ.
